docs.publisher:
The leading organization token. Copublishers follow after a slash;
the whole tail captures as ONE scalar span ("/IEC/IEEE") because
the engine's array-group harvest pads non-firing reps with empty
hashes (parsanol-ruby#399) — the builder splits the span.
docs.copublishers:
At least one item: the optional around [copublishers] keeps the
key absent when the identifier has no copublisher (a zero-width
capture would bind an empty array, not a scalar span).
docs.part_modern_body:
number/part bodies inlined at every capture site so each capture
holds one scalar span; part_legacy's negative lookahead keeps a
"/Amd"-style tail from being read as a legacy slash part.
docs.supplement_second_part_isor: ISO/R supplement layer second_part: isor_supp_* names.
docs.supplement_second_part: First supplement layer: /Amd 1:2021 after the base designation.
docs.supplement_second_part3: Third supplement layer (/Cor1:2014 riding a two-level chain): supp3_*.
docs.directives_supp_publisher: Non-bundled directives supplement (ISO/IEC DIR 1 ISO SUP): dsupp_*.
docs.directives_base_document:
Bundled directives ("DIR 1:2022 + IEC SUP:2022"): the base document
keeps the plain names, and each bundle item captures into its own
position-scoped prefix (bs1_* on the first, bs2_*/bs3_* on the
second and third). The engine's array-group harvest pads non-firing
reps with empty hashes (parsanol-ruby#399), so bundle items cannot
collect through an array binding; three items bound. The source
parser's 1* accepted any count — a fourth "+ SUP" item now fails
to parse rather than mis-bind.
docs.idf_supp_type_with_stage:
IDF supplement side of the joint (a true IDF supplement keeps its
fields under idf_supp_*2 names).
docs.identifier:
The ISO identifier root: common-text twin form first, then the
single spine.
